title.en: Respect the stability limit of an explicit scheme

summary: Check the declared explicit scheme and boundary discretization against its stability condition; use the one-dimensional diffusion bound only in its stated regime.
objective: Prevent a field simulation from producing growing oscillations that look like physics.
applies_when: A one-dimensional diffusion field uses forward Euler with centered spatial differences on a uniform grid and constant positive diffusivity.
Resolution, timestep or diffusivity changes within that model require rechecking the diffusion number.
For another explicit scheme, equation, dimension or boundary discretization, derive its own amplification condition before applying a timestep bound.
example_prompts: Simulate heat diffusion that stays stable when I refine the grid.
Show what happens when the time step is too large.
negative_signals: Implicit or spectral schemes, which have different stability behaviour.
Analytic solutions evaluated directly, where no stepping occurs.
not_for: Implicit or spectral schemes, which have different stability behaviour.
Analytic solutions evaluated directly, where no stepping occurs.

principles: Explicit schemes are conditionally stable, and the familiar limit belongs to one specific scheme. For the forward-Euler update with centred differences on a uniform one-dimensional grid with constant positive diffusivity, the time step must keep the diffusion number at or below one half. Two- and three-dimensional grids, variable coefficients, other boundary discretisations, wave equations and implicit schemes each have their own condition, and a zero diffusivity makes the limit undefined rather than infinite.

Violating the limit means susceptible modes are amplified rather than damped, which the reference run at a diffusion number of about zero point five three shows as a solution that blows up. It is not a guarantee that every run visibly explodes: a uniform field stays uniform, and a short run may end before the growth is visible. Below the limit, an initially rough field is also not required to look smooth immediately.
The quadratic dependence has a strong practical consequence: halving the grid spacing requires quartering the time step, so a resolution control silently multiplies the cost and can cross the limit.
Because instability is fast and obvious once you know its signature, it is better exposed with a warning than hidden by clamping the field values.
implementation: Validate positive finite spacing and the declared diffusivity regime, then compute the bound for the actual scheme and boundary treatment. Handle zero diffusivity as a separate no-diffusion case without dividing by it; do not reuse this bound for a different equation.
Recompute the limit whenever resolution or the coefficient changes, and adjust or refuse the change with an explanation.
Display the current stability number so the viewer can see the margin.
Do not clamp field values to hide divergence; report the instability and let the viewer see the characteristic growing oscillation.
Offer an implicit or smaller-step alternative when the explicit limit makes the interaction impractical, and say which scheme is running.
observable_checks: Choose a nonzero perturbation whose amplification factor under the actual grid and boundary scheme is known. Compare parameter choices for which its factor has magnitude below one and above one over a declared horizon; expect decay and growth respectively. A constant state does not test an unstable mode.
Refine the grid and confirm the step is reduced automatically by the expected factor.
Confirm the displayed stability number matches the parameters actually used.
Verify a stable run conserves or decays the field appropriately rather than accumulating high-frequency noise.

Alternatively evaluate the amplification factor of the scheme for the modes on your grid and confirm its magnitude is at most one; that is a direct check of the condition rather than a wait for visible failure.

creative_affordances: Deliberately showing an unstable run is an excellent teaching device when labelled.
The visual encoding of the field, from colour to displacement, is unconstrained by the stability rule.
known_limits: Authored numerics guidance citing the stability condition for the explicit scheme applied to one-dimensional diffusion; other equations, dimensions and schemes have different conditions.
No simulation has been run for this record, so no numerical result is asserted.

claims.statement: For the uniform-grid forward Euler scheme with centered spatial differences for one-dimensional diffusion, the cited analysis gives the diffusion-number bound F = diffusivity times timestep divided by grid spacing squared at or below one half. Stability requires the relevant mode amplification factors to have magnitude at most one; violating that condition amplifies susceptible modes, without requiring every initial state or finite run to visibly blow up.
claims.scope: One-dimensional constant-positive-diffusivity scheme under the boundary treatments analyzed by the source. Other discretizations require their own mode or matrix analysis; the bound is not a claim about every explicit method or every observed trajectory.

source_refs.locator: Sections 10.2.1 and 10.2.2: eigenvalue and Fourier-mode amplification criteria, forward Euler diffusion-number bound; section 10.2.3 blow-up example
